nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of WO3@CFC
nodes.procedure: First, 0.625 g tungstic acid powder was dissolved in 20 ml of 12 wt% hydrogen peroxide solution. Second, the mixture was heated at 95 °C with magnetic stirring for 3 h. Then, the solution was transferred into an 80 ml Teflon reaction kettle with 0.2 g anhydrous sodium sulfate, 115 μl hydrochloric acid and a piece of CFC (2 cm × 2 cm) added in. The obtained mixture was heated at 180 °C for 12 h, and then was washed using deionized water.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of WO3@CFC: The WO3 nanoplates on CFC were synthesized by the hydrothermal method. First, 0.625 g tungstic acid powder was dissolved... then was washed using deionized water.

nodes.name: Thermal reduction to def-WO3@CFC
nodes.procedure: The above prepared WO3@CFC was thermally treated to get def-WO3@CFC at 200 °C for 2 h in reducing gas flow (containing 5 vol% hydrogen and 95 vol% argon) in a tube furnace.
nodes.source_text: First, the above prepared WO3@CFC was thermally treated to get def-WO3@CFC at 200 °C for 2 h in reducing gas flow...

nodes.name: Deposition-precipitation of Pt/def-WO3@CFC
nodes.procedure: The def-WO3@CFC was immersed in 25 ml ammonium carbonate solution (1 M). ~0.5 g H2PtCl6·6H2O solution (2 wt%) was dissolved in 24 ml deionized water, and then added into the stock solution dropwise. The CFC was taken out for drying after aging for varied time durations (t) in the mixture solution, and it was found that 1 h of ageing in the solution is optimal for the highest catalytic activity. Finally, the Pt/def-WO3@CFC was obtained through further thermal treatment at 200 °C for 2 h under the same reducing gas (containing 5 vol% hydrogen and 95 vol% argon) in a tube furnace.

nodes.evidence_snippet: From the powder Xray diffraction (XRD) patterns of the prepared catalysts (Fig. S1†), WO3 in the catalyst is approximately of triclinic phase structure (PDF#20-1323).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows WO3 nanoplates growing perpendicularly on CFC fibers with negligible morphology change after oxygen vacancies introduction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning electron microscopy (SEM, Fig. S3a†) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM, Fig. S3b†) images demonstrate the successful synthesis of WO3 nanoplates.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals highly dispersed Pt atom clusters as bright dots on def-WO3 nanoplates surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: There are highly dispersed bright areas and dots on the surface of def-WO3@CFC after Pt species being loaded, implying the successful preparation and loading of Pt atom clusters (Fig. 2a and b).

properties.description: High-resolution image showing elongated nanostructures with uniform morphology

nodes.characterization_summary: Spherical aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM shows Pt atom clusters of 2-3 nm and directly visualizes oxygen vacancies as small red-marked circles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The relatively uniform dispersion of Pt atom clusters on the WO3 nanoplates can be further verified by the spherical aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM imaging as shown in the circled marked bright areas of 2-3 nm in size in Fig. 3a.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice fringes with interplanar spacings of 0.374 nm and 0.365 nm corresponding to (002) and (020) planes of triclinic WO3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the meantime, the lattice fringes in HRTEM (Fig. 3b) can be found with the measured interplanar spacings of 0.374 nm and 0.365 nm corresponding to the (002) and (020) planes of triclinic WO3.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mappings show no significant aggregation, confirming homogeneous dispersion of Pt atom clusters on def-WO3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: There is no significant aggregation observed in the elemental mapping images of Pt/def-WO3@CFC shown in Fig. 2e, further confirming the highly homogeneous dispersion of Pt atom clusters on def-WO3.

nodes.characterization_summary: ESR shows resonance peak at g=2.005 evidencing oxygen vacancies in def-WO3@CFC with slight intensity decrease after Pt loading.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The resonance peak at the g value of 2.005 evidences the presence of oxygen vacancies in a relatively low amount according to its intensity.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Pt 4f shows peaks at 72.4 eV (4f7/2) and 75.8 eV (4f5/2) consistent with Pt2+; W 4f shows peaks at ~36.0 eV (4f7/2) and ~38.4 eV (4f5/2) for W(VI) slightly shifted lower due to oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Pt 4f7/2 and 4f5/2 peaks of Pt/def-WO3@CFC are at 72.4 eV and 75.8 eV, respectively, which are consistent with the values of Pt2+... For def-WO3@CFC and Pt/def-WO3@CFC samples, two major peaks located at ~36.0 eV and ~38.4 eV belong to 4f7/2 and 4f5/2 of W(VI).

nodes.characterization_summary: Normalized W L3-edge XANES shows peak at ~10212 eV with increased intensity for Pt/def-WO3@CFC vs WO3@CFC, indicating oxygen vacancies make central W atom site more non-centrosymmetric.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Normalized W L-edge XANES of the three samples are resolved in Fig. 4e. The identically positioned peak at ~10212 eV can be seen for WO3@CFC and Pt/def-WO3@CFC... Compared with non-defective WO3@CFC the peak intensity of Pt/def-WO3@CFC increases significantly.

nodes.characterization_summary: W L3-edge EXAFS shows W-O shell at R=1.38 Å and W-Pt shell at R=1.93 Å confirming Pt occupation of oxygen vacancy sites in contact with W atoms.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectra (Fig. 4f) show the short-range (below 4 Å) local structure of W in the as-prepared samples, indicating the presence of one W–O shell (R = 1.38 Å) and one W–Pt shell (R = 1.93 Å) around an atomic W site in Pt/def-WO3@CFC.
